turns.content: Draw 3,3,6-trimethylhepta-1,5-dien-4-one and distinguish its terminal alkene from its conjugated enone alkene.
With one equivalent of mCPBA, identify the two possible monoepoxide branches, one from each alkene.

Excess dimethylcuprate is generated from methyllithium and CuI. For each monoepoxide branch, predict epoxide-opening regiochemistry, any conjugate addition to a remaining enone, and the fate of the ketone carbonyl.
After aqueous workup, identify one resulting product by systematic name and defining functional groups.
Verify its origin from attack at the less substituted epoxide carbon and conjugate addition where applicable, without direct addition to the ketone carbonyl.
Report the product name and the branch-specific reaction sequence.
